KR.read: Korea's emerging adjacencies now has data for two of six taxonomy sub-segments. Beauty_devices: US$1.32bn (2024, RETAIL, LOW confidence, Expert Market Research), a home/consumer device scope (acne, hair-removal, cleansing, oxygen/steamer, rejuvenation devices) that may overlap professional aesthetic devices; this is a sub-segment figure only, not a segment total. Ingestible_nutricosmetics: ~KRW 1.0tn in 2023 (~US$0.676bn, RETAIL, MEDIUM confidence, Shinhan Financial Investment Research via Seoul Finance), up from ~KRW 0.7tn in 2019 - though this 'inner beauty' market is sold as health-functional food in Korea, so it sits outside the conventional BPC retail perimeter and should not be added to BPC totals without flagging that risk. The other four sub-segments (halal_certified, ayurvedic_herbal, clean_vegan, kbeauty_derivative) have no Korea data.
KR.trend: Beauty_devices carries the fastest verified KR adjacency growth: a LOW-confidence 13.8% CAGR (2025-2034, Expert Market Research) - roughly 2.5x the pace of KR skincare or hair care - plus a MEDIUM-confidence company-level proxy of +44.6% YoY for 2024 (APR Corp's AGE-R brand, NET_REALISATION basis, company earnings announcement), used because no clean same-source category-wide two-year series could be found; APR is Korea's largest listed home beauty-device player, so this is a leading-indicator proxy, not a market-wide rate. Ingestible_nutricosmetics shows a historical +9.3% CAGR (2019-2023, ESTIMATE, derived from two endpoints on the same source) against a much more aggressive company projection of KRW 2.0tn by 2025 (MEDIUM confidence, same source) that would imply roughly 41% CAGR from 2023 - a projection well above the observed historical trend, not (yet) an outturn.
KR.caveats: Both sub-segment growth figures for beauty_devices are proxies (a forecast CAGR and a single company's revenue growth), not an observed category-wide rate. The nutricosmetics 2025 projection (KRW 2.0tn) is a sell-side forecast from 2024 that implies a sharp acceleration off the observed 2019-2023 trend and has no verified 2025 outturn on file. Four of six taxonomy sub-segments remain entirely without Korea data.

IN.read: India's emerging adjacencies now has data across five of six taxonomy sub-segments. Ayurvedic_herbal: the cleanest BPC-scoped figure is IMARC's ayurvedic-skincare-only read at US$2.0bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW) - this excludes ayurvedic oral care and colour cosmetics, so it under-covers the adjacency; a wider, ESTIMATE-confidence derived figure of INR 42,735cr (~2.2x the skincare-only figure) covers skin, oral, hair and fragrances, with the same publisher's organised/unorganised split (70%/30%, 2025) applied. Halal_certified: US$1.3bn (2025, RETAIL, LOW, IMARC), organised/unorganised coverage not stated, and the category is inherently hard to audit since halal certification in India has no single national register. Clean_vegan: INR 7,786.49cr (~US$0.81bn, 2025, RETAIL, LOW, Expert Market Research), a publisher-defined 'clean' boundary with no Indian regulatory basis. Beauty_devices: two closely-agreeing LOW-confidence figures on an identical personal-care-appliance scope (trimmers, dryers, straighteners, epilators) - IMARC US$2.1bn (2025) and TechSci US$1.81bn (2024) - unusually consistent for a pair of aggregators, though this is a grooming-appliance basket, not the at-home skincare-device (LED mask, microcurrent) reading the taxonomy targets. Kbeauty_derivative [CORRIDOR]: two LOW-confidence figures directly contradict each other - MarkNtel US$310mn for 2025 versus Credence Research's higher US$406.58mn for the earlier year 2023, an outright contradiction on a category both describe as growing.
IN.trend: Growth reads vary sharply by sub-segment and scope. Ayurvedic: skincare-only forecasts 11.98% (2026-2034, LOW, IMARC) while the wider personal-care-plus-non-BPC-healthcare basket forecasts 15.52% (2026-2034, LOW) - the latter is 58% healthcare/medicine by the source's own breakdown and should not be applied to the BPC adjacency. Halal: 7.28% (2026-2034, LOW, IMARC); a MarkNtel figure reportedly near 30% could not be verified on a fetched page and is not recorded. Clean_vegan carries both a forecast (15.7% CAGR, 2026-2035, LOW) and an observed company read: Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth) reported 20% YoY revenue growth for FY26 (HIGH confidence, BSE regulatory filing) - company-level across Honasa's full portfolio, not a category-wide clean/vegan market rate, since no market-wide series exists. Beauty_devices CAGRs also agree closely (14.56% IMARC vs 15.56% TechSci, both LOW). Kbeauty_derivative CAGRs diverge on top of the size contradiction: 18.06% (MarkNtel) vs 10.00% (Credence Research), both LOW, both [CORRIDOR]-tagged.
IN.caveats: The ayurvedic wider-basket growth rate (15.52%) is majority non-BPC and must not be quoted as a BPC growth figure. The kbeauty_derivative pair is a genuine contradiction, not just a gap - a later year reading lower than an earlier year on a category both sources describe as growing - so neither figure should be treated as settled; grey-market/parallel-import K-beauty is a known unmeasured channel that likely means both undercount actual sell-through. The Honasa 20% figure is a diversified-portfolio company result (Mamaearth plus six other brands, some dermatology-positioned rather than clean/vegan) standing in for a sub-segment with no market-wide series. Organised/unorganised coverage is stated only for the wider ayurvedic estimate (70%/30%); it is unstated elsewhere.

combined.read: A KR-vs-IN comparison is only possible sub-segment by sub-segment, and even then is limited: beauty_devices is the one sub-segment with a size figure on both sides, but the scopes differ (Korea: home devices including oxygen/steamer/rejuvenation; India: personal-care grooming appliances including trimmers and hair dryers), so a direct value_usd_bn comparison would compare different baskets, not the same market. Kbeauty_derivative is [CORRIDOR]-tagged in India (US$310-407mn, contradictory across two sources) with no Korea-side counterpart figure recorded for this specific sub-segment. No other sub-segment has data on both sides. Given the scope mismatches and one-sided coverage, no aggregate KR-vs-IN emerging-adjacencies comparison is attempted here.
